mx.teacher_note: classification as a fluid happens first, and that produces ability to flow and lack of fixed shape.

mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Applies to both liquids and gases even though a liquid has fixed volume and a gas does not is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Liquids and gases are fluids because they flow and do not retain a fixed shape; solids are distinguished from them by retaining a definite shape. ability to flow and lack of fixed shape -> classification as a fluid The learner classifies liquids and gases as fluids because they flow and lack fixed shape, while solids are not fluids merely because many grains can be poured. Anything that can be poured is a liquid or fluid, even if it is made of many solid grains.
